chunks: Because al-‘Ays ibn al-Qasim narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him about a man who performs ghusl for ihram in al-Madīnah, wears two garments, then sleeps before entering ihram. He said: “There is no ghusl upon him.”
And whoever performs ghusl at the beginning of the night, then enters ihram at the end of the night, his ghusl suffices him.

key_terms.أَحْرَمَ: he entered into the state of ihram
key_terms.الْإِحْرَامِ: the state of consecration for hajj or ʿumrah
key_terms.ثَوْبَيْنِ: the two garments worn for ihram
key_terms.غُسْلٌ: ritual bath required or discussed in this ruling

ai.seo_question: Does sleeping after ghusl for ihram require repeating the ghusl before entering ihram?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about ghusl for ihram. It indicates that sleeping after performing ghusl for ihram does not require repeating the ghusl, and that a ghusl done earlier in the night remains sufficient for entering ihram later that night.
